::: {.callout-warning}
## Before you connect anything

**Pinch points on the micrometer stage.** A micrometer stage closes a gap
between two hard surfaces under mechanical advantage, and fingers belong
nowhere in that gap while the spindle is turning. Keep hands clear of the
stage's moving faces, wind slowly, and never force the spindle past a hard
stop — a stalled stage and a pinched finger are the same failure with
different consequences.

**Suspended masses, again.** The on-the-beam cross-check of
@sec-m2-step-crosscheck hangs the same reference masses M1 uses. The same
warning applies unchanged: never put a hand or an instrument under a
suspended mass, load one mass at a time, and never exceed the beam's working
load — see [M1's safety
callout](../M1-strain-load/handbook.qmd#sec-m1-procedure) for why exceeding
it invalidates every relation this experiment depends on, not just M1's.

**The sensor supply.** Verify the Hall sensor's supply voltage with a DMM
before powering it — a ratiometric sensor's output is only meaningful
relative to the supply it actually received, and an out-of-spec supply can
damage the part before it ever produces a reading worth analysing.
:::

### 1. Identify the board {#sec-m2-step-identify}

```bash
arduino-io list
arduino-io info
```

As in [S1](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-identify): write down
`adc_bits`, `vref_mV` and whether `streaming` is available.

### 2. Calibration sweep: the magnet on the micrometer stage {#sec-m2-step-sweep}

With the Hall sensor fixed and the magnet mounted on the micrometer stage,
sweep the distance from close (strong signal, strong curvature) to far
(weak signal, nearly flat), recording both the sensor output and the supply
voltage together:

```bash
arduino-io mode 15 analog && arduino-io mode 16 analog
# d = 2 mm
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/cal-d0002.csv
# ... repeat at each distance in the sweep, working outward
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Record the micrometer reading, not a nominal step

Write the micrometer's own reading into `channels[].reference_value`, not
the distance you intended to move to — backlash and any zero offset in the
stage mean the two are not the same number, and the whole calibration fit
depends on knowing which one you have.
:::

### 3. Supply-voltage drift, displacement held fixed {#sec-m2-step-drift}

Hold the stage at the working point chosen from @sec-m2-window (see the
analysis template), and record a longer run while deliberately varying the
supply voltage — a bench supply's coarse adjustment, or simply its own warm-
up drift over a longer recording, whichever your bench can produce
controllably:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 500 --seconds 20 --csv data/supply-drift.csv
```

Nothing about the displacement changes during this run. Whatever the raw
Hall-output channel shows changing is the supply, not the target — which is
exactly the point @sec-m2-supply exists to make with real numbers.

### 4. On the beam: the stiffness cross-check {#sec-m2-step-crosscheck}

Mount the Hall sensor and its magnet at the beam tip, at the baseline gap
chosen from the working-range analysis, and apply the same small set of
reference masses [M1 uses](../M1-strain-load/handbook.qmd#sec-m1-step-bridges)
for its quarter-bridge sweep:

```bash
arduino-io stream 15,16 --hz 1000 --seconds 0.2 --csv data/crosscheck-000.csv
# ... repeat for each reference mass, same set M1 used
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Use the same masses M1 used

The stiffness cross-check of @sec-m2-crosscheck compares two independent
measurements of the same loading. If M2's masses do not match M1's exactly,
the comparison is between two different experiments, not a cross-check of
one.
:::

### 5. Fill the sidecars {#sec-m2-step-sidecar}

Beyond the fields [S1](../S1-daq-static/handbook.qmd#sec-s1-step-sidecar)
already asks for:

- [ ] `channels[].reference_value` / `.reference_u` — the micrometer reading
      (calibration sweep) or the applied force in newtons (cross-check runs)
- [ ] Both pins present in `acquisition.pins` and described in `channels[]`
      — the Hall output and the supply-voltage sense, every run
- [ ] `synthetic: false`
